subject: Renewal: smoothing thresholds + commit rebalance playbook
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Dobson <pdobson@bluecrest.ai>, Sara Li <sara.li@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: smoothing thresholds + commit rebalance playbook

Paul / Sara —

Thanks again for the time last week. Based on your usage profile for the past 9 months, we sketched two non-disruptive renewal paths that keep your per-token economics predictable while removing cliff effects during usage spikes. Attached is a short summary (renewal_summary_v1.pdf). High level: 

- Option A: 12m committed volume with a 3-month smoothing window for thresholds; quarterly true-ups.
- Option B: 12m commit with monthly true-up but a 20% uplift ceiling to limit bill volatility.

We want to avoid introducing heavy paperwork on your side, so both options keep pricing simple (per-token tiers) and add a clear uplift guardrail. Questions we have for you: which cadence do you prefer for true-ups (monthly vs quarterly), and do you need an explicit cap on uplift above forecast?

If you prefer, we can produce an example invoice cadence and a one-page contract amendment for your procurement team.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: renewal_summary_v1.pdf
From: Paul Dobson <pdobson@bluecrest.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:03:47 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: smoothing thresholds + commit rebalance playbook

Thanks Jonas —

PDF looked good at a glance. Two quick asks from our side: 

1) Can you show an explicit worked example showing how the 3-month smoothing would apply to a spike in month 2 (we had a pilot spike in July that worries procurement).
2) Procurement wants to avoid open-ended overage exposure. Could you propose a maximum annual uplift (percent) that caps our worst-case bill for planning?

If you can send the worked example and a proposed uplift ceiling we can loop in legal.

—Paul
Head of Product | Bluecrest Analytics
pdobson@bluecrest.ai

Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:22:15 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal: smoothing thresholds + commit rebalance playbook

Paul —

Quick worked example inline and a proposed uplift ceiling: 

Example (3-month smoothing, Option A):
- Month 1 actual: 90k tokens (baseline)
- Month 2 actual: 210k tokens (pilot spike)
- Month 3 actual: 110k tokens
- 3-month moving average used as effective usage for threshold calculation: (90k + 210k + 110k)/3 = 136.7k
- True-up invoice compares committed monthly equivalent to moving average; overage billed at the overage per-token tier but subject to the uplift cap.

Proposed uplift ceiling: 25% annualized (we can lower to 20% if you prefer stronger predictability). The ceiling applies to cumulative overage charges versus committed spend for the 12m term; it’s a hard cap on excess invoicing, not on throughput.

Additional notes:
- We can add a minimum floor (e.g., 85% of historical run-rate) to avoid rollback risk.
- For contracts, we can deliver a simple amendment that preserves your existing terms and adds the smoothing clause.
- If you’re planning to migrate to Redwood Dedicated in year 2, we can include a migration credit tied to committed spend.

I attached a short spreadsheet with the worked math (smoothing-examples.xlsx) and a one-page term summary. Happy to walk it through on a quick call.

—Karthik
Director, Renewals | Redwood Inference
CC: Marissa for commercial approval

Attachment: smoothing-examples.xlsx
From: Sara Li <sara.li@bluecrest.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Dobson <pdobson@bluecrest.ai>, Finance Team <ap@bluecrest.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:06:02 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: smoothing thresholds + commit rebalance playbook

Karthik —

Thanks for the worked example — that helps. Procurement/legal have a few comments before we can sign: 

- Remove auto-renew; we’ll agree to a 12m term but require manual renewal at end of term.
- True-up mechanics look fine but we want a firm maximum uplift ceiling of 20% (not 25%).
- We need a guaranteed per-token ceiling (a top tier price that cannot be exceeded for the term).
- Can you confirm SOC2 in-scope evidence and whether audit logs will be available for our compliance team? 

If you can accept the 20% uplift cap and confirm the security artifacts, we’ll prepare a PO and route for signature.

Best,
Sara Li
Procurement Lead | Bluecrest Analytics
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@bluecrest.ai>, Paul Dobson <pdobson@bluecrest.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:14:31 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal: smoothing thresholds + commit rebalance playbook

Sara —

Appreciate the clear list. Summary of Redwood’s proposed compromise: 

- Term: 12 months, no auto-renew (manual renewal at term end) — agreed.
- Uplift cap: 20% annualized hard cap on cumulative overage charges — accepted.
- Per-token ceiling: we will lock the top-tier per-token price for the 12m term and include an explicit per-token ceiling clause in the amendment.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II report and scoped audit artifacts + access to token-level logs for the contract term — we will provide a redacted evidence bundle via our secure portal and a point of contact for audit requests.

Next steps: I’ll have Legal prepare a 1-page amendment that incorporates the smoothing language, the 20% uplift cap, and the per-token ceiling. Karthik, can you include the migration credit language (low priority) and finalize the amendment? I’ll also drop a DocuSign link for signature once legal has a clean version.

Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
